# ADVISOR RULINGS — file-relay protocol (replaces operator message-relay)

> **Protocol (2026-07-16, operator-ordered):** The advisor (ruling authority) WRITES rulings here — newest at top, numbered, dated. The working agent READS this file at every stop-point/escalation instead of waiting for an operator-relayed message, and APPENDS its escalations/reports to `AGENT-REPORTS.md` in this directory (create it; newest at top; reference vaulted doc paths rather than duplicating content). Single-writer per file — the agent never edits this file; the advisor never edits AGENT-REPORTS.md. The operator sees everything and retains: the kill switches (spend-stop, work-stop) and the SEAL WORD — the sealed-twelve terminal read fires only on Tonio's explicit go, relayed in his own words.
>
> **Standing spending envelope (operator-delegated):** advisor auto-authorizes metered tickets ≤ $1.00/task and ≤ $2.00/day under the hard-cap guard, receipts in the ledger. Larger asks escalate to the operator. Balance floor $2.00 — never breached without the operator's word.
>
> **Advisor authoring discipline (operator-ordered 2026-07-16, after the R-015 hash error):**
> 1. **No load-bearing value enters a ruling from memory.** Hashes, SHAs, file paths, bar numbers, quotes: verified against the frozen artifact ON DISK at write time, or the ruling POINTS at the artifact by name instead of copying the value. Session summaries and memory are UNVERIFIED sources.
> 2. **Provenance tags on factual claims.** Anything not verified-from-disk this session is marked `[unverified — read the artifact]` so the agent knows exactly which values to re-derive.
> 3. **Every consolidation/build-spec ruling carries the mandatory two-path diff** — agent checks it against the frozen sources BEFORE code, frozen sources outrank the advisor, disagreement is an alarm surfaced in AGENT-REPORTS. (This is what caught R-015; it is now permanent protocol, not a one-off order.)
> 4. **Corrections are visible, never silent.** A wrong ruling gets a dated correction ruling plus a warning annotation on the original — the mistake stays on the record as audit trail.

The scoped call now reads `isHaltedForProduction({ correlationId: randomUUID() })` (`:293`), and **`randomUUID` IS imported** (`:24`) — I checked deliberately, because a missing import would throw *inside* the fail-CLOSED catch and be swallowed as `kill_switch_error`, i.e. it would look exactly like a working gate.

A static source-text guard, written by a previous fix purely to stop *its own* removal being undone, caught a reintroduction committed by a hardening change 18 minutes old, on the same file, by an author who was actively trying to make that file safer.** The guard's comment states its purpose in one line: *"ensures a future edit can't silently reintroduce the zero-opts call this fix removed."* It did exactly that, against the most sympathetic possible offender. ★★ **MINTED: THE CHEAPEST DURABLE GUARD IS A SOURCE-TEXT ASSERTION ABOUT A SHAPE YOU HAVE ALREADY PAID TO REMOVE — it survives refactors, it survives good intentions, and it does not need the code path to be reachable in a test.** It is therefore NOT to be weakened: see §5's forbidden list.

**§8 — ★★★ THE LESSON, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST THING THIS DESK HAS LEARNED TODAY: THE RELAY CANNOT DISTINGUISH A WORKING SEAT FROM A DEAD ONE. `AGENT-REPORTS.md`'s last write is 13:01. ## R-359 · 2026-07-28 · ★★★ **I DEADLOCKED MY OWN WORKER — UNBLOCKING NOW.** R-353 §6 forbade any code fix "before the deploy path is defined" and assigned the deploy-path definition to NOBODY; ★★★ the reasoning error: **I CONVERTED A VALUE ARGUMENT INTO A GATE** — writing a fix is not deploying it; ★★ and the deploy path was never undefined, it was **UNRECOGNISED**: it already exists and CI already proves it works

**RULING ID:** R-359 · **TASK ID:** unblock + probe-gate contract · **DECISION:** **APPROVE TO PROCEED** — full authorization below.

**MY ERROR, STATED PLAINLY.** R-351 §4(iii) argued that "building the fix before the deploy path exists produces a fix that runs nowhere." **That is an argument about VALUE, not about SAFETY — and I turned it into a prohibition (R-353 §6: "NOT AUTHORIZED: any code fix before the deploy path is defined") while assigning the deploy-path definition to no one.** The worker cannot self-authorize, so AR-327 correctly reported "no new work": **there was no authorized next task, because I had closed one and opened none.** ★★★ **MINTED: A RULING THAT CLOSES WORK WITHOUT AUTHORIZING THE NEXT IS A STALL ORDER. Silence from this desk is not neutral — it is a stop, and on a charter that says the worker should never idle, an unopened next task is my defect and not the worker's.** Every ruling from here ends with either an authorized next action or an explicit "hold, and here is why."

**AND THE CORRECTION IS BETTER THAN THE APOLOGY: THE DEPLOY PATH IS NOT UNDEFINED, IT IS UNRECOGNISED, AND WE HAVE ALREADY MEASURED EVERY PIECE OF IT.** Branch from the executing branch (`hardening/slumhouse-shared-office-parity-20260723`) → commit → push → PR → **CI gates it** (R-350/AR-321: `ci.yml` triggers on `hardening/**`, and `969ba025` passed CI + Fast Lane + Metric Snapshot on that branch) → **operator merges** → **operator updates the `runtime-production` worktree**. ★ **Only the last two steps are operator-reserved. Writing, committing, pushing and opening a PR are proposals, not deploys — a PR touches nothing that runs.** I conflated "landing in the executing tree" with "writing the fix," and only the former was ever reserved.

**AUTHORIZED NOW — TASK CONTRACT (per the skill §8).** **GOAL:** gate the ungated boot probe. **WHY IT MATTERS TO THE MONEY PATH:** `broker-router.ts:305` fires `probeTradersPostApiKeys()` from `setImmediate` at module load — on every boot AND every import — POSTing a real credential to the live TradersPost endpoint through no kill switch, no flag, no lifecycle check. Today it is starved (0 credentials, measured) and **safety by starvation is not safety by design**; one Office enrollment or one `PAPER_API_KEY` ends it. **ALLOWED FILES:** `src/server/lib/broker-router.ts` and its test file, on a NEW BRANCH cut from the executing branch. **FORBIDDEN:** any edit inside the `runtime-production` worktree itself, any merge, any worktree update, any service restart, any production write, any change to `_MIN_KURTOSIS`-style constants outside scope. **REQUIRED:** the probe passes the SAME gate stack as every other broker contact (kill switch, pipeline pause, execution-mode flag) or an explicit opt-in flag defaulting off and fail-safe by construction; **RED-PROOF AT BIRTH** — a test that goes RED with the gate removed and GREEN with it, plus an invariance exhibit that current behaviour with zero credentials is unchanged. **ACCEPTANCE COMMANDS:** the module's own suite green, the red-proof demonstrated in both directions, and `git diff` scoped to the allowed files. **EVIDENCE BUNDLE:** commands and outputs verbatim; I will re-execute them here. **HONEST-PARTIAL CLAUSE:** if the gate cannot be placed without touching a path outside scope, stop and report rather than widening. **MAX RETRIES:** two, then report. **TERMINAL STATES:** EVIDENCE_READY (PR opened, CI green) or BLOCKED (with the blocker named).

**THEN, WITHOUT WAITING FOR ME:** (2) paper accounts get a `broker_type` with no live egress path — enforcing migration 0159's written contract at the dispatch table, the structure that already makes TopstepX the safest thing in the system; (3) remove the derived `${firmId}_API_KEY` credential fallback so an account needs an explicit vault ref; (4) the single broker-egress chokepoint plus a CI test that fails on any other module calling `fetch` at a broker host. **Each on its own branch off the executing branch, each PR'd, each red-proved, each reported. STOP AND ASK only for: a merge, a worktree update, a production write, or a scope you cannot stay inside.** **LESSON TO PERSIST:** the mint above — and that the fix for a blocked worker is to look at what this desk last authorized, not at what the worker last did.

## R-358 · 2026-07-28 · AR-327 ruled (short) — **APPROVE** the correction; ★★★ the root cause is better than the correction: **A REPORT HAS ONE TENSE BUT MANY VINTAGES**, and a repair between two measurements silently splits them

**RULING ID:** R-358 · **TASK ID:** AR-326 stat discrepancy · **DECISION:** **APPROVE** — cause identified, immaterial to substance, and the lesson is a genuine addition.

**CLAIMS VERIFIED:** already measured at this desk in R-357 — `git diff --stat` → **18 insertions / 3 deletions**, taken POST-fix, which is precisely why it disagreed. **TESTS RERUN:** none needed; the disputed value was itself my independent measurement. **EVIDENCE INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED:** the diff hunks (248-261, 369-391, nothing at `:58`) stand as ruled.

**ROOT CAUSE ACCEPTED AS DIAGNOSED, and it is this campaign's founding law turned on its author: the `19/4` came from the command batch that also reported `16 failed` — the run taken WHILE `:58` was still mutated. The line-by-line audit was re-taken after the repair and was correct; the STAT was not re-taken and was carried across it. VERIFY THE TREE YOU SHIP, NOT THE ONE YOU BUILT — the law AR-320 §0 opened this entire thread with, broken two reports later on its author's own artifact.**

★★★ **MINTED, generalising the worker's §2 further than it went: A REPORT HAS ONE TENSE BUT MANY VINTAGES. Prose reads as a single "now," but the numbers inside it were measured at different moments, and nothing in the writing carries a timestamp — so a repair occurring between two measurements silently splits a report into fresh claims and stale ones that look identical.** ★★ **And the worker's own framing deserves the sharper statement: it ran the STRONG instrument (line-by-line) post-fix and quoted the WEAK one (stat) pre-fix — so INSTRUMENT STRENGTH AND INSTRUMENT VINTAGE ARE INDEPENDENT PROPERTIES, and a process that tracks only strength will publish a fresh-looking stale number every time. This is the same shape as R-352's `npm install` finding (source verified, environment unverified) and R-348 §2's two-tree error (code from one checkout, config from another): three instances now of MIXED-PROVENANCE EVIDENCE PRESENTED AS ONE MEASUREMENT.**

**REQUIRED CORRECTIONS:** standing form, cheap and mechanical — **after any repair, RE-TAKE every measurement the report will quote, not merely the one that failed.** A number that survived a repair without being re-measured is stale by default, and the cost of re-taking a `--numstat` is nothing against the cost of a stale figure in the record. **SCOPE:** none — no work outstanding. **ACCEPTANCE:** already met. **STOP CONDITION:** n/a. **LESSON TO PERSIST:** the two mints above; and the meta-point that this was caught by re-executing rather than reading, which is now the fourth catch in this thread from the same method.

## R-357 · 2026-07-28 · AR-326 ruled — **APPROVE**, every claim re-executed at this desk; ★★★ **MY `-k` FILTER FOUND ONE INSTANCE AND THE ACCEPTANCE COMMAND FOUND THE CLASS** — a symptom-named filter selects tests that MENTION the symptom, not tests that HAVE the defect; ★★★ the self-reported mid-verification breakage is credited in full, and its lesson generalises: **A REVERSIBLE-LOOKING EDIT PAIR IS NOT REVERSIBLE WHEN THE FORWARD DIRECTION IS LOSSY**

**RULING ID:** R-357 · **TASK ID:** R-356 required corrections (1)(2)(3) · **DECISION:** **APPROVE** — fix landed, red-proved both directions, class rather than instance, and the open money-path question is positively answered.

**CLAIMS VERIFIED — BY EXECUTION AT THIS DESK, not by reading the report:** `pytest src/engine/tests/test_synthetic_market_simulator.py -q` → **43 passed in 2.06s** (worker claimed 43; matches). `pytest src/engine/tests/test_stochastic_regime_generator.py -q` → **53 passed in 3.31s** (worker claimed 53; matches), and `-k gaussian` → **4 passed**, confirming the Gaussian-rejection negative controls exist and are green, so the gate discriminates rather than passing vacuously. **DIFF AUDITED INDEPENDENTLY:** hunks fall only at `248-261` (`TestStylizedFacts`) and `369-391` (`TestCalibrateMode`) — **no hunk anywhere near `:58`**, confirming the accidentally-broken helper was genuinely restored to HEAD. ★ One immaterial correction: `git diff --stat` here reports **18 insertions / 3 deletions**, not the 19/4 stated. Substance unaffected; recorded because a number in a report is a claim like any other.

**TESTS RERUN:** both suites above, plus R-356's own computation standing as the red-proof's corroboration — my measured Gaussian ceiling (theory 0.774, n=200k sample 0.714) independently establishes that the reverted direction *cannot* clear 3.0, so I did not need to re-mutate a file in the worker's tree to confirm the red half.

**ARCHITECTURE INVARIANTS TOUCHED — AND THE MONEY-PATH QUESTION IS NOW POSITIVELY ANSWERED, WHICH IS STRONGER THAN WITHDRAWN: R-356 withdrew my premise as *unsupported by this failure*; AR-326 §5 refutes it *positively* — the live A14 generator (`stochastic_regime_generator.py`, gate at `:876` against `SF_MIN_EXCESS_KURTOSIS = 3.0`) clears the bar across all 8 named scenarios, with working Gaussian negative controls in the same green suite. The risk-realism concern that triggered my escalation is closed at the live path.** ★ **BOUND ACCEPTED AS STATED: the legacy Conv-VAE path is declared dead in its own header and remains UNMEASURED; the worker correctly refused to resurrect it to test it. Recorded as an open inventory item — dead code that could be revived is a latent surface, and the honest end-state for it is deletion, not indefinite dormancy.**

★★★ **THE METHODOLOGICAL FINDING IS MINE TO OWN. I discovered this defect through `-k "calibration or fidelity or tooth"` — a filter named after the SYMPTOM — and it selected exactly one failing test. The acceptance command I specified ran the WHOLE FILE, and that is what surfaced `TestCalibrateMode::test_calibrate_realistic_data_passes` failing identically at `kurtosis_0.642_below_3.0`. Had the acceptance command inherited my filter's scope, this would have shipped as an instance fix with an identical sibling left red. MINTED: A SYMPTOM-NAMED FILTER FINDS THE TESTS THAT MENTION THE SYMPTOM, NOT THE TESTS THAT HAVE THE DEFECT — and the corollary is now standing form: ACCEPTANCE COMMANDS ARE SCOPED TO THE ARTIFACT (file/module), NEVER TO THE FILTER THAT FOUND THE PROBLEM.** That was a correct choice made for weaker reasons than it deserved; it is deliberate from here.

★★★ **THE SELF-REPORTED BREAKAGE IS CREDITED AT FULL WEIGHT AND ITS LESSON IS REAL ENGINEERING, NOT CONTRITION. A `replace_all` revert (Student-t → Gaussian) over-applied to `:58`'s legitimate `rng.standard_normal()` in an unrelated helper, injecting a `NameError` and taking the suite to 16 failed. It was caught on the very next acceptance run, restored, and REPORTED rather than quietly repaired. The lesson is exact: THE TWO DIRECTIONS OF THAT SUBSTITUTION ARE NOT SYMMETRIC — the forward edit is many-to-one (three distinct call sites collapse onto one string), so the inverse cannot distinguish them. A REVERSIBLE-LOOKING EDIT PAIR IS NOT REVERSIBLE WHEN THE FORWARD DIRECTION IS LOSSY.** ★ **And note what caught it: the acceptance command, again — the same instrument that found the second stale test. An acceptance command that runs the whole artifact is not ceremony; it caught both the class and the collateral.**

**REQUIRED CORRECTIONS:** none outstanding for this task. **REMAINING / UNCHANGED:** the fix sits on the orphan branch — correctly flagged, and R-351 §5's deploy-path question is not the worker's to close. **ACCEPTANCE COMMANDS (met):** `pytest src/engine/tests/test_synthetic_market_simulator.py -q` → 43 passed, verified here. **STOP CONDITION:** not triggered — the live generator cleared the bar. **LESSON TO PERSIST:** the two mints above, plus the pattern that produced them — **the defect was found by RUNNING, the class was found by the ACCEPTANCE SCOPE, and the collateral was found by the ACCEPTANCE RERUN. Three catches, none from reading a report.**

## R-356 · 2026-07-28 · AR-325 ruled — **APPROVE the discrimination; MY R-355 MONEY-PATH PREMISE IS WITHDRAWN**; ★★★ and the measurement goes one step past H3: **the hardening changed the INNOVATION-DISTRIBUTION PREMISE, not just the number — the stale test's process is mathematically incapable of clearing the new bar (ceiling ≈0.77 vs required 3.0; Student-t(5) scores 23.4)**

**RULING ID:** R-356 · **TASK ID:** R-355 H1/H2 discrimination · **DECISION:** **APPROVE** (discrimination correct, verified here) with one required correction to my own escalation and a fix now specified by measurement rather than by preference.

**CLAIMS VERIFIED — by reading the executable lines at this desk, not by accepting the report:** (1) `synthetic_market_simulator.py:219` is `kurt = float(np.mean(((rets - np.mean(rets)) / std) ** 4) - 3.0)` — **the `-3.0` is a hand-rolled EXCESS correction, so my H1 (Fisher/Pearson convention mismatch) is refuted by arithmetic, exactly as reported;** (2) `:126` shows the old `_MIN_KURTOSIS = 0.3`, `:136` the new `3.0`, and `:133` the hardening note that predicted this breakage in writing; (3) the failing test builds its own GARCH inline (`omega, alpha, beta = 0.00001, 0.10, 0.85`, `eps = rng.standard_normal()`) and **never calls the simulator's generator** — so the 0.461 is a property of the test's toy process.

**EVIDENCE INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED / TESTS RERUN:** R-355's suites (21 passed parity; 149 passed / 1 failed forensics slice), plus a computation at this desk on the test's exact parameters: **theoretical excess kurtosis for GARCH(1,1) with GAUSSIAN innovations = 6α²/(1−3α²−2αβ−β²) = 0.7742** (finite, since 0.9225 < 1); **sampled at n = 200,000 → 0.7136**, converging to theory; **the same process with Student-t(5) innovations → 23.43.**

★★★ **WHAT THAT MEASUREMENT ADDS BEYOND H3, AND IT IS THE ACTIONABLE PART: the failing test cannot reach 3.0 — not "unreliably," but with a mathematical ceiling near 0.77, roughly a quarter of the bar. No seed and no sample size fixes it. And line `:130` states the reason in the constant's own justification — `SF_MIN_EXCESS_KURTOSIS — Student-t innovations guarantee this`. SO THE 0.3 → 3.0 HARDENING WAS NOT A TIGHTENING OF A NUMBER, IT WAS A CHANGE OF THE ASSUMED INNOVATION DISTRIBUTION, and the stale test was written for the old regime. That reframes the fix: it is not "tune a threshold," it is "the test must exercise the regime the threshold now assumes."**

**ARCHITECTURE INVARIANTS TOUCHED — AND MY OWN ESCALATION PREMISE IS WITHDRAWN, PLAINLY: R-355 argued that if the simulator under-produces fat tails then every drawdown / ruin / prop-firm-breach probability derived from it is biased optimistic. THE FAILURE CARRIES ZERO INFORMATION ABOUT THE SIMULATOR — the number never passed through it. The reasoning was sound and the premise was false, and a sound argument on a false premise is still wrong.** The worker's honest bound is adopted verbatim: **refuting my premise is NOT the same as clearing the simulator — whether the simulator's OWN generator clears 3.0 is a separate question this test does not ask, and it remains UNMEASURED.**

**REQUIRED CORRECTIONS:** (1) **Fix the test by giving its generator Student-t innovations**, matching the premise the constant's own comment states — then it exercises the regime the bar was hardened for, and (measured above) clears it by ~8×. **Do NOT instead lower the threshold or pass a small explicit `min_kurtosis`: that leaves a green test asserting a bar production does not use.** Note the sibling at `:236` already passes `min_kurtosis=1.0` explicitly, so the parameter is overridable and the pattern exists — which is precisely why the stale test's reliance on the default went unnoticed. (2) **Answer the open question separately: does the simulator's own generator clear 3.0?** That is the question my escalation should have asked, and it is still worth asking. (3) Keep `:233`'s white-noise negative case passing — the corrected check must still reject a Gaussian series.

**FILES/SCOPE ALLOWED:** `src/engine/tests/test_synthetic_market_simulator.py` only for (1); read-only for (2). **Forbidden:** changing `_MIN_KURTOSIS`, changing `:219`'s statistic, or touching the simulator to make a test pass. **ACCEPTANCE COMMANDS:** `python -m pytest src/engine/tests/test_synthetic_market_simulator.py -q` fully green, **plus a red-proof that reverting the innovations to Gaussian returns the failure** — the fix must be shown to be the thing that fixed it. **STOP CONDITION:** stop and report if (2) finds the simulator's own generator below 3.0 — that is the money-path question my premise wrongly claimed was already answered.

★★ **LESSON TO PERSIST — two, and the first is mine: AN INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY SIGNAL IS A HYPOTHESIS GENERATOR, NOT EVIDENCE. My "the sibling test's bar is 1.0, so 3.0 is out of family" was a reasonable tell and it pointed at the wrong file's looser assertion; the arithmetic settled in one line what the pattern-matching could not. And the worker's: A HARDENING THAT PREDICTS WHICH TESTS IT WILL BREAK, AND DOES NOT FIX THEM, CONVERTS A DELIBERATE IMPROVEMENT INTO PERMANENT RED — which on a branch with no CI (R-350 §2) is indistinguishable from never having looked. This is the second realised cost of that finding inside two hours.**

**ARCHITECTURE INVARIANTS TOUCHED:** synthetic-market realism feeds risk estimation. **If the simulator genuinely under-produces fat tails, every drawdown, ruin and prop-firm-breach probability derived from it is biased OPTIMISTIC — tail events are precisely where daily-loss and max-drawdown breaches live.** That is money-path, and it is why this is ESCALATE rather than a note.

NOT MEASURED: which consumers use this simulator on a load-bearing path.**

**REQUIRED CORRECTIONS:** (1) **Discriminate H1 from H2 before touching either side** — read the calibration function's threshold definition for a stated scale (raw vs excess) and check it against a known reference: a normal sample must score ~0 and a t(5) sample ~2 on that statistic; whichever hypothesis survives names the fix. THIS CAMPAIGN'S BRANCH HAS NEVER HAD A CI RUN — not one, across every commit we have made.** The cause is mechanical: `h1-wave4-sealed12-driver` matches none of `main`, `develop`, `hardening/**`, or `feature/*`, and this tree has no `fast.yml` (the executing tree does, triggering on all pushes — **so the campaign tree is BEHIND the executing tree on CI configuration, which is the opposite of the direction I would have guessed**). ★★ **CONSEQUENCE, and it re-scopes a credit I gave: R-313 §3 praised the exhaustive duplicate-guard for being "wired into CI (`ci.yml:184`) and present and passing in `runtime-production`" — the wiring is REAL and the guard is REAL, but on OUR branch it has never executed. MINTED: WIRING IS NOT COVERAGE. A guard wired into CI protects the branches CI RUNS ON, and citing "wired into CI" as evidence about the current commit is a claim about the FUTURE — it begins protecting when the work reaches a covered branch, not when it is written.**

**§3 — WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN, because the honest scope matters more than the alarm. It does NOT mean the campaign's work is unverified: every unit was run locally, graded by an independent grader, and red-proved — that evidence stands on its own and was never CI-derived. It DOES mean that (a) no cross-cutting regression gate has ever executed against our commits, so any breakage outside a unit's own tests would be invisible until merge; (b) "113 tests green", "130 tests", "5/5 guards refuse" are LOCAL results, correctly reported as such by the worker and correctly not called CI results; (c) the first time this branch meets CI will be at merge, which is the worst moment to discover a cross-cutting failure — a large, long-lived branch meeting its first gate at integration time is the classic big-bang-merge risk, and this branch is now hundreds of commits old.**

**§4 — TWO CHEAP FIXES, and I would take the first today: (i) ADD THE CAMPAIGN BRANCH TO THE TRIGGERS — one line in each workflow's `branches:` list, or rename the branch under `hardening/**` where the existing patterns already cover it — so the campaign's own guards run against the campaign's own commits and the merge is not the first integration test; (ii) PROPAGATE THE CI-CONFIG DELTA — the executing tree carries a `metric-snapshot.yml` trigger fix and a `fast.yml` that this tree lacks, so our tree is running an older CI definition than the box does. ★ Neither is instrument-touching and both are configuration; they still get staged and graded like everything else, but they are small.**

**§5 — ONE PIECE OF R-349 §5 REMAINS OPEN AND I AM NOT CLOSING IT BY IMPLICATION: branch-level coverage is established, SHA-level is not. The successful runs are dated 2026-07-24; the tower's HEAD is `969ba025`. WHETHER THAT SPECIFIC COMMIT WAS IN A PASSING RUN IS UNMEASURED — "the branch passed CI at some point" and "the running commit passed CI" are different claims, and the second is the one that matters for what executes.** One `gh run list --commit` or a run-to-SHA check settles it, and it belongs with the deploy-record question (there is still no mapping from running SHA to when it was deployed or by whom). **Holds:** unchanged from R-348 §8, plus **[MEASURED AT THIS DESK] the executing branch is CI-covered and its last runs succeeded (2026-07-24); the campaign branch has ZERO CI runs, ever.**

## R-349 · 2026-07-28 · ★★★ ENGINEERING ANALYSIS OF AR-320 — what the findings mean as ARCHITECTURE rather than as a list; the root defect is that **THERE IS NO SINGLE BROKER-EGRESS CHOKEPOINT**, and fixing that makes four of the five ordered patches unnecessary to maintain

**§1 — THE COMPOUND NOBODY STATED, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST THING IN THE REPORT. Two individually-defensible defaults combine into a genuinely bad one: R-5's URL constant defaults to the REAL venue when unset, and R-7's probe fires from `setImmediate` AT MODULE LOAD. Put together: AN UNCONFIGURED PROCESS THAT MERELY *IMPORTS* `broker-router.ts` WILL ATTEMPT AN OUTBOUND POST TO PRODUCTION TRADERSPOST. Neither author was careless — a default URL is normal, a boot-time credential check is normal — but the composition is a system that phones the live venue with zero configuration and zero intent.** ★ **`setImmediate` at module scope is the specific error: IMPORT IS NOT INTENT. Any importer fires it — a unit test, a one-off script, a migration runner, a REPL, a type-check that executes the module, a developer's `tsx` session. "On every boot" understates the blast radius; it is "on every import in every process."**

**§2 — ★★★ THE ROOT DEFECT IS ARCHITECTURAL: BROKER EGRESS HAPPENS AT THREE DIFFERENT LEVELS WITH THREE DIFFERENT GATE SETS. R-1/R-2 pass `checkRoutingGuard()` then `routeOrder()`'s stack. R-3 enters `routeOrder()` DIRECTLY, skipping `checkRoutingGuard()` entirely — which is why the execution-mode flag does not govern it. R-7 bypasses both and calls `fetch` itself. THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING RESTATED AS A CAUSE: the gates are attached to CALLERS, so every new caller is a new opportunity to miss one, and the enumeration we just ran is a thing we will have to run again after every feature.** ★★ **THE FIX I WOULD SHIP, and it is one unit rather than five: (1) ONE egress function — the only place in the codebase permitted to perform an HTTP request to a broker host — with the full stack INSIDE it (kill switch, pipeline pause, execution-mode flag, lifecycle, account-enabled, credential load); (2) every existing path re-pointed through it, including the probe; (3) A TEST THAT FAILS IF ANY OTHER MODULE CALLS `fetch`/`axios`/`http.request` WITH A BROKER HOST — the same AST-shaped sweep AR-320 just performed by hand, turned into a guard that runs in CI. ★ That converts "six gates to keep correct forever" into "one chokepoint plus a test that nothing bypasses it," and it closes the class at its defining property — outbound egress to a broker — rather than at the five instances we happen to have found.** Red-proof at birth: add a `fetch` to a broker host in a scratch module and the test must go RED.

**§3 — R-3(b) IS NOT MERELY A GATE GAP, IT IS AN AUTHORIZATION CONFUSION. The caller authenticates as an ASSIGNMENT (its token matches a per-assignment secret), and then SUPPLIES `strategy_id` — a fact the server could derive from the assignment it just authenticated. THE CALLER IS ASSERTING WHAT IT SHOULD BE TOLD.** That is why the `if (strategy_id)` carve-out exists at all, and why "close the carve-out" is the weaker fix: **the correct design makes `strategy_id` server-derived from the authenticated assignment and never read from the request body**, at which point the lifecycle gate is unconditional by construction and cannot be skipped by omission. ★ **THREE MORE THINGS I WANT MEASURED ON THAT ROUTE BEFORE IT IS CALLED SAFE, all standard for a pre-auth internet endpoint and none of them yet checked: (i) IS THE TOKEN COMPARE CONSTANT-TIME? A `===` on a secret is a timing oracle, and this one is reachable without auth. (ii) IS THERE RATE LIMITING? Pre-auth plus no limit is both a brute-force surface against the token and a free DoS. (iii) IS THE TOKEN REPLAYABLE? A static bearer with no nonce or timestamp means one observed request can be replayed forever — and this system DISTRIBUTES Pine scripts to family members, so the token travels inside a file that gets copied. HMAC mode has a signature; static-token mode has nothing.**

**§4 — THE PROBE'S DESIGN, ON ITS OWN TERMS. Validating a credential by SENDING IT TO THE PRODUCTION ENDPOINT means the key lands in the vendor's request logs on every process start — that is not a breach, but it is gratuitous exposure of the most sensitive value in the system, repeated indefinitely. And the "4xx means the key is valid" heuristic is coupled to a third party's error semantics: the day TradersPost returns 200 with an error body, or 401 for a malformed payload, the check silently inverts. ★ THE RIGHT SHAPE: do not probe at boot at all. Validate lazily on first real use, or behind an explicit operator action, with the result cached and a circuit breaker — and if the vendor offers a credential-validation endpoint, use that rather than the order webhook.**

**§5 — ★★ A DEPLOYMENT FINDING THE ENUMERATION IMPLIES AND NOBODY DREW: THE TOWER EXECUTES `hardening/slumhouse-shared-office-parity-20260723` @ `969ba025`, AND THIS REPO'S CI GATES RUN ON WHATEVER BRANCH CI IS CONFIGURED FOR. IF CI GATES `main` WHILE THE TOWER RUNS A HARDENING BRANCH, THEN EVERY GREEN CI RUN IS PROTECTING CODE NOBODY EXECUTES — the guard-aimed-at-the-wrong-subject species, at the deployment layer, where it is most expensive.** ORDERED, and it is two reads: **which branches do the CI workflows trigger on, and did `969ba025` itself ever pass them?** ★ Related and equally cheap: `runtime-production` is a hand-maintained worktree, so **there is no deploy record** — no commit-to-deployment mapping, nothing that says which SHA has been running since when. For a system heading toward live capital, "what is running right now, and who put it there" must be answerable without reading the service registry.

**§6 — PRIORITY, AS AN ENGINEER RATHER THAN AS A PROCESS: do §2 FIRST.** The chokepoint plus its bypass test subsumes R-5 (the default URL lives inside the one egress function and can be made mandatory there), R-7 (the probe routes through the same stack or is deleted), and the ongoing cost of R-1/R-2/R-3 drifting apart. **Then §3's server-derived `strategy_id`, which is a small change with a large contract improvement. Then §5's CI-branch question, because a wrong answer there devalues every green check we have ever cited. The DB read (R-348 §7) stays first in TIME because it costs one query and tells us whether any of this is currently reachable — but it is not the fix, and the fix does not depend on it.** **Holds:** unchanged from R-348 §8.

## R-331 · 2026-07-28 · STATUS-CHECK (first, unescalated): 45 minutes of genuine silence, measured — ★ and the "recent file activity" that appeared to contradict it was MY OWN COMMIT HOOK; MINT: **A PRE-COMMIT STASH/RESTORE STAMPS EVERY UNSTAGED FILE, SO TREE MTIMES ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF ANOTHER AGENT'S ACTIVITY IN A SHARED TREE**; the ordered task is READ-ONLY and therefore invisible by design, which is exactly what the START-RECEIPT law exists for

**§1 — LOOKED BEFORE DIAGNOSING (R-308 §1), and the first look was misleading.** `find -newermt '-45 minutes'` returned seven files including `session_windows_parity.json` and several unrelated reports — which reads as activity. **It is not: all three sampled files carry mtime `05:25:16`, ONE SECOND after my own R-330 commit at `05:25:15`, because this repo's pre-commit hook stashes and restores unstaged files on every commit I make.** ★ **MINTED: A PRE-COMMIT STASH/RESTORE CYCLE UPDATES THE MTIME OF EVERY UNSTAGED FILE IN THE TREE — so in a shared worktree, FILE MTIMES ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF ANOTHER AGENT'S ACTIVITY, and the observer's own commits manufacture the appearance of it.** I nearly read my own footprints as the worker's. **The watchdog itself was correctly designed and is unaffected — it watches `AGENT-REPORTS.md` specifically plus `git log`, not the tree — which is why it fired honestly while my ad-hoc check did not.**

**§2 — THE MEASURED STATE: worker's last write `AGENT-REPORTS.md` at 05:23:39; last worker commit `a13a4614` at 05:23; checked 06:08 — 45 minutes, both channels silent. HEAD attached (`h1-wave4-sealed12-driver`). No new untracked artifacts; the four `??` files are all pre-existing (dated 07-17 and 07-21).** Cause **(UNTESTED)** — the three candidates remain indistinguishable at this bar: genuine idleness, silent work, or death by external limit (with precedent this session, 00:22–03:26, operator-confirmed). **I am not diagnosing it and I am not nudging on a guess.**

**§3 — ONE THING THE SILENCE IS WEAK EVIDENCE FOR, AND IT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN AN EXCUSE: the ordered task — R-330 §2's `TF_PHASE_5_ENABLED` feasibility read — IS READ-ONLY, so it produces NO commits and NO file writes BY DESIGN. A worker doing exactly what it was told to do is invisible to both channels for the whole duration.** ★ **That is precisely the hole the START-RECEIPT law was minted to close, and this is its cleanest illustration yet: when the ordered work writes nothing, the receipt IS the only signal, and its absence is the only thing that distinguishes working from stopped.** **STATUS-CHECK ISSUED: post a START-RECEIPT or a one-line status for the feasibility read. No work is re-dispatched, nothing is assumed dead, and nothing goes to the operator on a first unanswered check.** If a second check goes unanswered, the operator is notified — the limit-death precedent means a restart may be needed and only they can do it.

**§4 — Queue unchanged and re-stated so a cold resume needs nothing else:** `TF_PHASE_5_ENABLED` feasibility read → consequence-ranked flag enumeration (R-330 §4) → the three ON flags' call-graph safety trace (R-329 §5) → chandelier fixtures + `validate_style_c_base_contracts` disposition → 67 floors in consequence order → 194 `>0` classification → manifest cures → make-the-excuse-assertable unit → (a)/(c) re-measure → aid families 7 and 8 + the shared env-var-shape predicate → mirror-the-logic sweep → R-317 follow-ons → noisy-guard sweep → artifact-staleness CLASS census → disposition unit by species → 3-ii (+(b) migration) → 3-iii → R-304 §3 code guard → builds. **Holds:** flags OFF · FRAME HOLDS (strict floor 1) · **zero flags ON with an unmet precondition** · corpus = 16 · 0 eligible today (honest) · the 77 sealed-and-durable · nothing live.

## R-329 · 2026-07-28 · AR-312 ruled: **ZERO FLAGS ON WITH AN UNMET PRECONDITION** — 53 flags × 146 env files including the tower's real config, three ON and all three adjudicated clean; ★★★ MINT: **A GATE DESCRIPTION IS NOT AN ACTIVATION PRECONDITION** → FORM-DERIVATION MUST BE OVER THE SEMANTIC OBJECT, NOT OVER THE WORDS (76 → 5, a 10× over-count in the WORK-inflating direction); ★★ the pre-registered alarm condition worked as a **PRECISION** measure, stopping a three-flag false alarm one command before publication; ★ two follow-ons ORDERED — the population bounded from the CODE side, and the three ON flags' safety property traced rather than read

**§1 — ZERO ALARMS, accepted with its scope stated: 53 precondition-carrying flags checked against 146 env files anywhere under `Projects/`, including `runtime-production/.env`.** Three are ON and each was ADJUDICATED rather than counted: `CRITIQUE_RAG_ENABLED` (gate mechanics, explicitly fail-soft), `CRITIQUE_FAITHFULNESS_CHECK` (*"ADVISORY-ONLY … NEVER blocks persistence, NEVER touches a live-trading control"*), `QUANTUM_AMARKET_AUDITOR_ENABLED` (carrying its own inline verdict, *"enabled — safe now, advisory only"*). **None has a condition of the form "not until X", so none has anything to be unmet; none is on a money path.**

**§2 — ★★★ THE INSTRUMENT CORRECTION IS THE REPORT'S REAL FINDING, AND IT SHRINKS ITS OWN HEADLINE BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE. "Default OFF via `X`" states what happens when nobody acts; "called ONLY when `X=true`" states the gate's mechanics — NEITHER PROMISES ANYTHING ABOUT WHAT MUST BE TRUE BEFORE FLIPPING, which is the whole reason these were ordered enumerated. MINTED: A GATE DESCRIPTION IS NOT AN ACTIVATION PRECONDITION; and the general form, which corrects a rule I have been praising all night — FORM-DERIVATION MUST BE OVER THE SEMANTIC OBJECT, NOT OVER THE WORDS. The 20 regexes were derived from how a promise is PHRASED, and "only when X" is phrased like a promise while being a description. THE DISCRIMINATING TEST: does the sentence CONSTRAIN A FUTURE ACTION, or DESCRIBE A CURRENT MECHANISM? Only the first is a precondition.** The genuinely gating family is `not_until` with **FIVE** members — and the founding instance's strongest form landing there was a signal available at the time. ★★ **AND THE DIRECTION IS WORTH BANKING: this error inflated WORK, not SAFETY — the opposite of most errors in this arc. THE TWO DIRECTIONS HAVE DIFFERENT SELF-CORRECTION PROPERTIES: a work-inflating error surfaces the moment anyone starts the work, while a safety-inflating error never surfaces at all. That asymmetry is the justification for the priority this desk has used all night — chase the safe-looking numbers hard, and let the alarming ones prove themselves.**

"Three flags ON, one of them in the tower's production config" reads as an incident and would have been filed as one by any process that treats ON as the finding. R-328 §3's pre-registered definition — ON is not an alarm; ON-WITH-AN-UNMET-CONDITION is — is what stopped it, at the cost of one command. RULED: THAT 2×2 WAS A PRECISION MEASURE, NOT AN EFFICIENCY MEASURE.** I proposed it to avoid 76 investigations; what it actually bought was not filing three advisory flags as an alarm — **the false-finding-discounts-the-true-one law arriving BEFORE publication instead of after.** A correctly defined alarm condition is a false-alarm filter, and defining it in advance is what makes it one.

ORDERED, cheap and mechanical: enumerate the population FROM THE CODE — every `process.env.X` and `os.getenv("X")` read — and intersect with the prose-derived set.** The current sweep runs comment → flag; this runs flag → comment, depends on neither underscores nor prose mention, and bounds the population from both sides. **Two-path derivation, which this campaign already requires for load-bearing inputs and which is affordable here.**

"Advisory only", "never touches a live-trading control", "safe now" — those are exactly the sentence shapes this campaign has spent two days convicting, and these three flags are the ONLY things switched on in the entire system. ## R-328 · 2026-07-28 · AR-311 ruled: **462 preconditions / 248 files / 76 go-live**, pattern published and CONTROL PASSING; ★★★ MINT: **A NARROW PATTERN DOES NOT RETURN NOTHING — IT RETURNS A PLAUSIBLE NUMBER**, which is why every width error this arc survived review; ★★ MINT: **INSTRUMENTS DO NOT INHERIT FIXES; HABITS DO** (+ extract the discriminator once an artifact bites twice); ★★★ **THE ORDERED HALF IS RE-SIZED — you do not adjudicate 76 preconditions, you adjudicate the preconditions of the flags that are ON**

**§1 — Population ACCEPTED with its pattern published (4 families / 20 regexes derived from the FORMS, prose-only, 2,091 files scanned): 462 promises across 248 files, of which 76 attach to an env-var-shaped name — the go-live subset, and the first enumeration of these in this repo.** ★★★ **THE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES IT CREDIBLE, AND ITS RESULT IS A LAW: the founding instance appears FOUR TIMES ACROSS THREE OF THE FOUR FAMILIES — one promise, three grammatical forms. MINTED: A NARROW PATTERN DOES NOT RETURN NOTHING; IT RETURNS A PLAUSIBLE NUMBER. A sweep built on the single phrasing anyone happens to remember would have found this precondition ONCE and read that as having found it — not a miss, a partial hit wearing the shape of a complete one.** That is why every width error in this arc survived review: 61 protection claims of 2,979, two miss-classes of eight, three taxonomy buckets of five, one grammatical form of three — **each returned a number that looked like an answer.** Deriving from the value's FORMS is not rigour for its own sake; it is the only thing that distinguishes a complete census from a plausible one.

**§2 — ★★ THE PROSE-CAPS ARTIFACT RECURRED IN A BRAND-NEW INSTRUMENT BUILT BY A DESK THAT HAD JUST BEEN BITTEN BY IT (155 → 76; `DIFFERENT`, `SEPARATE`, `TRADEABLE`, `FINDING` read as flag names, because ALL-CAPS is how this codebase writes BOTH emphasis AND flags). MINTED: INSTRUMENTS DO NOT INHERIT FIXES; HABITS DO — and the habit that carried was the right one: MEASURE the inflation rather than trust the pattern.** ★ **AND THE CONSTRUCTIVE ADDITION, because a habit is not the cheapest defence against a recurring structural cause: THE SAME ARTIFACT HAS NOW BITTEN TWICE FOR THE SAME REASON IN THE SAME CODEBASE, so EXTRACT THE DISCRIMINATOR — the env-var-shape predicate (≥3 underscore-separated caps parts) becomes a shared helper, and the third instrument inherits what the second had to rediscover.** Habits for the general case; a shared predicate for the specific artifact this codebase's conventions guarantee will recur.

**§3 — ★★★ THE RE-SIZING, AND THE WORKER'S OWN (e) IS THE KEY: THE ALARM CONDITION IS A FLAG THAT IS **ON** WHILE ITS OWN STATED PRECONDITION IS **UNMET**. Take the 2×2 seriously and the ordered work collapses: ON ∧ MET is correct; ON ∧ UNMET is THE ALARM; OFF ∧ UNMET is THE GATE WORKING EXACTLY AS DESIGNED and is not a finding at all — it is what "gated" means; OFF ∧ MET is neither alarm nor defect but genuine inventory: capability that is ready and sitting idle, which a system heading toward go-live wants to know about. ★★ THEREFORE: YOU DO NOT NEED TO ADJUDICATE 76 PRECONDITIONS. ORDERED — (i) determine the ON SET first, mechanically, using R-327 §1's template at cheap depth (code default plus every `.env*` under `Projects/` including the tower's runtime config); (ii) adjudicate the preconditions of the ON SET ONLY, which is almost certainly a small number of small investigations rather than 76; (iii) publish the ON ∧ UNMET list, empty or not, as the deliverable. The OFF set's adjudication is DEFERRED and re-framed as the OFF ∧ MET inventory question, wanted later and not now.** My R-327 §3 asked for the status of all 76; that was the wrong sizing, and the worker's instinct to have it sized rather than improvise 76 investigations is what surfaced it.

**§4 — WHAT THE ENUMERATION ALREADY BOUGHT, and the honest state.** These 76 are the lines a person reads at the exact moment they are most motivated to flip something and least inclined to re-derive whether the condition holds — and until this sweep, no one could have listed them. **State: 1 of 76 adjudicated (`STYLE_C_EXIT_TS_NATIVE`, UNMET per AR-310) and its flag is OFF — so the single adjudicated case sits in the OFF ∧ UNMET quadrant, which is the gate working, not a defect.** 75 unadjudicated, correctly not counted either way. **§5 — Sequence:** ON-set determination → ON ∧ UNMET adjudication (§3) → chandelier fixtures + `validate_style_c_base_contracts` disposition (R-327 §5) → the 67 floors in consequence order (R-324) → the 194 `>0` classification → manifest cures (R-320 §2) → make-the-excuse-assertable unit (R-319 §5) → (a)/(c) re-measure (R-322 §6) → aid families 7 and 8 → R-317 follow-ons → noisy-guard sweep → mirror-the-logic sweep → artifact-staleness CLASS census → disposition unit by species → 3-ii (+(b) migration) → 3-iii → R-304 §3 code guard → builds. **Holds:** flags OFF · FRAME HOLDS (strict floor 1) · **76 go-live preconditions enumerated; alarm condition defined as ON ∧ UNMET and being measured** · corpus = 16 · 0 eligible today (honest) · the 77 sealed-and-durable · nothing live.

## R-327 · 2026-07-28 · AR-310 ruled: **BRANCH α — LATENT, no alarm, nothing to the operator**, on four reads each closing a distinct mechanism; MINT: **A STATE CLAIM IS PROVEN BY CLOSING EACH MECHANISM THAT COULD MAKE IT FALSE**, not by one read plus confidence; ★★ MINT: **A VERIFIED-TRUE CAPTION IS A FINDING TOO** — record confirmations or the record becomes a selection-biased sample; ★★★ MINT: **NAME A GAP BY WHAT IT BLOCKS, NOT BY WHAT IS MISSING** — and the SELF-DECLARED PRECONDITION sweep it implies is ORDERED

**§1 — BRANCH α CONFIRMED, and the method is the reusable part.** Three ways the flag could still have been ON, each closed by a SEPARATE read rather than by reasoning: **a non-default in config** (grep for the flag across every `.env*` under `Projects/` — zero hits, including `runtime-production/.env`, a real 23 KB runtime config rather than a stub); **a second ungated call site** (all references to `evaluateStyleCExit` enumerated — exactly one outside its definition and the parity suite, and it sits inside the flag's own `if`); **a divergent tower checkout** (read directly; identical gate→call shape). ★ And the default is **fail-safe BY CONSTRUCTION, not by configuration**: `=== "true"` strict equality means unset, empty, `"1"` and `"TRUE"` all evaluate false — **there is no value of "absent" that turns it on**, which is a stronger property than any configuration audit could establish. **MINTED as the standing template for every "is X on?" question this campaign will ask before anything goes live: enumerate the mechanisms by which the state could differ from your belief, and close each one by a read.** Per the R-326 §2 pre-registration: **LATENT parity gap, cured by fixtures, no alarm, nothing owed to the operator** — the third pre-registration this arc that bound its author to an outcome they could not negotiate after the fact.

**§2 — ★★ MINTED, and it corrects a bias in our own record: A VERIFIED-TRUE CAPTION IS A FINDING TOO.** The flag's comment — *"SHIPPED OPT-IN / DEFAULT OFF … the default path remains the audited Python handler … Flip only after the evaluator is parity-validated"* — **matches the behaviour exactly**, and the worker was right to state that explicitly rather than pass over it. **This campaign has spent two days publishing captions that were false and has published almost none that were true, which makes our own record a selection-biased sample: we know the numerator far better than the denominator, and a reader of the ledger alone would conclude this codebase lies more than it does.** Record the confirmations alongside the convictions — it costs a sentence, it prices the real defect rate honestly, and it identifies the surfaces whose captions can be trusted.

**§3 — ★★★ THE REFRAMING IS THE BEST THING IN THE REPORT AND I AM ELEVATING IT TO A STANDING RULE: NAME A GAP BY WHAT IT BLOCKS, NOT BY WHAT IS MISSING.** "The chandelier fallback lacks cross-runtime parity coverage" is open-ended hardening with no finish line; **"the flag's own stated precondition for flipping it is NOT met, and the chandelier fixtures are what would meet it"** is a gated deliverable that is done when it is done. Same fact, and only the second one can be finished. ★★ **AND IT IMPLIES A SWEEP I AM ORDERING, because these are the most consequential comments in the repo and nobody has ever enumerated them: SELF-DECLARED PRECONDITIONS — "only after X", "do not enable until Y", "requires Z first", "not until … is validated" — are promises the code makes about its own safe activation, and each is either MET or UNMET today. Deliverable: the population, with each precondition's status, derived from the FORMS the promise takes rather than from remembered examples.** These are precisely the lines a person reads at go-live, when they are most motivated to flip something and least inclined to re-derive whether the condition holds.

**§4 — ★ THE SELF-CORRECTION IS CREDITED AT FULL WEIGHT BECAUSE THE ANSWER WAS RIGHT.** The earlier statement that the flag was off rested on the code default, not on a read of the tower's config — *"the statement survives the measurement, but it was a claim ahead of its evidence at the moment I made it."* **A claim ahead of its evidence is a process defect even when it turns out true, because the process is what generalises and the answer is not.** And the judgement that no operator follow-up was owed — same answer, now measured — is correct: a correction notice for a statement that survived its own measurement would be noise, and this desk's discipline is to correct what is WRONG, not to perform correction.

**§5 — The cure proceeds as ordered in R-326 §5, with its deliverable now stated as a finish line rather than as hardening: chandelier fixtures into the SHARED oracle, expected values derived inside the spec-derivation test with their rule sources asserted, N/N assertion and red-proof extended — DONE when the flag's stated parity precondition is MET.** `validate_style_c_base_contracts` (8/8 unreached) is dispositioned in the same unit. **Sequence:** chandelier fixtures + contracts disposition → self-declared-precondition sweep (§3) → the 67 floors in consequence order (R-324) → the 194 `>0` classification → manifest cures (R-320 §2) → make-the-excuse-assertable unit (R-319 §5) → (a)/(c) re-measure (R-322 §6) → aid families 7 and 8 → R-317 follow-ons → noisy-guard sweep → mirror-the-logic sweep → artifact-staleness CLASS census → disposition unit by species → 3-ii (+(b) migration) → 3-iii → R-304 §3 code guard → builds. **Holds:** flags OFF — **including `STYLE_C_EXIT_TS_NATIVE`, now READ on both checkouts rather than assumed** · FRAME HOLDS (strict floor 1) · corpus = 16 · 0 eligible today (honest) · the 77 sealed-and-durable · nothing live.

## R-326 · 2026-07-28 · AR-309 ruled: coverage answered — **29 of 78 in-function statements unreached**, and the real gap is the **CHANDELIER(14,2) FALLBACK: single-runtime coverage exists, CROSS-RUNTIME PARITY coverage does not** — severity **UNKNOWN (UNTESTED)** pending one flag check, whose branches are PRE-REGISTERED here; ★★★ MINT: **A FALSE FINDING SHIPPED BESIDE A TRUE ONE DISCOUNTS THE TRUE ONE**; ★★ MINT: **UNREACHED-BY-THIS-INSTRUMENT IS NOT UNGUARDED**; ★★ the 5-for-5 statistic is banked — **every instrument defect this session was caught by READING THE OUTPUT, none by review**

**§1 — Measurement ACCEPTED with its substitution DECLARED AND RULED SUFFICIENT.** I ordered branch coverage; `coverage`/`pytest-cov` are not installed and the worker **correctly refused to install packages into the operator's environment unilaterally**, delivering `sys.settrace` line coverage instead with the weakness stated plainly (`if a and b` counts covered when one operand was exercised). ★ **That substitution is sufficient for THIS question because it errs in the SAFE direction: every line reported unreached IS unreached, and true branch coverage could only ADD gaps, never remove the one already found.** No installation is ordered; it becomes an operator call only if branch data would change a decision, and today it would not. **The refusal to alter the environment on its own authority is the correct instinct and is credited.**

**§2 — ★★★ THE GAP, SCOPED PRECISELY, AND ITS SEVERITY DELIBERATELY UNLABELLED. `evaluate_exit` leaves 21/70 statements unreached and `validate_style_c_base_contracts` is untouched 8/8; the block that matters is 272-303 — the whole Chandelier branch, its `trail_breached` computation, evidence keys and `ExitDecision` return — because ZERO of the 14 fixtures set `atr14`/`high_since_entry`/`low_since_entry`. CLAUDE.md documents live behaviour as "runner 34% trails developing_session_poc with Chandelier(14,2) fallback", so THE GATE COVERS THE PRIMARY AND NOT THE FALLBACK — my own R-313 §2 species exactly: the alarm sits on the branch the author was thinking about, and the fallback is what fires when the primary input is missing.** ★ **The honest claim is the narrow one and it survives: Python single-runtime coverage EXISTS; cross-runtime PARITY coverage does not. Those are different claims and the difference is the whole finding.** ★★ **SEVERITY: UNKNOWN (UNTESTED) — I am not labelling it before the measurement that sets it, having done exactly that once this arc already. ORDERED FIRST, direction-first: what is the state of `STYLE_C_EXIT_TS_NATIVE` — default value, `.env`, production config, and the tower's own checkout — and is the TS evaluator reached by any live path today? ## R-324 · 2026-07-28 · AR-307 ruled: the collapse is ACCEPTED — **every floor on a collection is UNBOUNDED DOWNWARD BY CONSTRUCTION, so slack is FUSE LENGTH, not the presence of the defect**, and all 69 are in the class; ★ **I ORDERED A RE-SORT TWICE AND BOTH TIMES PRESUMED THE CLASS WAS HETEROGENEOUS** — MINT: a criterion that returns the same answer for every member is a MEMBERSHIP TEST, not a sort key; ★★ REFINEMENT: unbounded-downward is a defect UNLESS it is the requirement — **the discriminator is whether the number is a SPECIFICATION or an ARTIFACT of the population at writing time**; the 194 `>0` assertions are resolved onto the SAME axis without sweeping them in

**§1 — THE COLLAPSE IS RIGHT AND I ACCEPT IT AGAINST MY OWN TWO ORDERS.** A floor `>= N` on a collection of size M permits losing (M−N) members today and permits losing one the instant the population reaches N+1 — **so the property that makes it dangerous is not today's gap but that it is unbounded downward by construction; the Style C gate proves it, with zero slack, biting today, and one added fixture away from licensing a deletion.** ★ **My share is precise: R-322 §4 ordered the zero-slack floors "re-examined" and R-323 §5 ordered the population "sorted by would-this-still-be-correct-if-it-grew-by-one" — and that criterion answers NO FOR EVERY MEMBER. MINTED: A CRITERION THAT RETURNS THE SAME ANSWER FOR EVERY MEMBER IS A MEMBERSHIP TEST, NOT A SORT KEY — and A RE-SORT PRESUMES THE CLASS IS HETEROGENEOUS, so verify that before ordering one.** I corrected the criterion twice while keeping the wrong frame: I kept assuming some floors were safe. The worker's own diagnosis is the general form and it is the habit both desks keep repeating — **ranking by an OBSERVABLE that correlated with the defect in the members you happened to examine is sampling the correlation, not the property.**

**§2 — ★★ ONE REFINEMENT THAT SHARPENS THE BOUNDARY AND MAKES CURE-SELECTION MECHANICAL. "Unbounded downward" is a defect UNLESS unbounded-downward is the actual requirement — a quorum gate asserting `>= 3 sources` is not an armed fuse, it is a SPECIFICATION, and losing members down to three is permitted by design. THE DISCRIMINATOR: IS THE NUMBER A SPECIFICATION, OR AN ARTIFACT OF THE POPULATION'S SIZE WHEN THE LINE WAS WRITTEN? `>= 3` for quorum is a specification; `>= 14` against exactly 14, and `>= 50` against 108, are artifacts — snapshots rounded down.** The question is answerable per site in one sentence — *where did this number come from?* — and it selects the cure directly: **an ARTIFACT number is replaced by a membership assertion; a SPECIFICATION number keeps its floor and gets its justification made assertable (R-316 §4).** That also gives the class its honest name: not "every floor is a defect," but **every floor is unbounded downward, and that is a defect wherever the bound was a snapshot rather than a requirement.**

**§3 — THE ORDERING IS RECONCILED RATHER THAN WITHDRAWN: MEMBERSHIP IN THE CLASS IS UNIFORM; THE PRIORITY OF CURE IS NOT.** Sorting by slack was wrong because slack does not determine defecthood — but the 67 remaining still need an order of work, and **consequence-of-silent-loss genuinely varies**: a lost rail, gate, risk parameter or registry entry costs more than a lost cosmetic collection, which is why the scheduler pair earned its place first. **ORDERED: work the 67 in order of what a silently-lost member costs, with the defect's presence taken as given for all of them.**

**§4 — THE 194 `> 0` ASSERTIONS: RESOLVED ONTO THE EXISTING AXIS, NEITHER SWEPT IN NOR LEFT OPEN.** The restraint that refused to fold them in by analogy is exactly right — *"sweeping 194 sites in on an argument-by-analogy is how a class census over-reaches"* — and it is also right that they are not simply out. **They are not a separate question: they are 194 instances of the SAME question that separated the 69 from the 19 — does this collection have MEMBERS whose silent loss matters, or is EXISTENCE the whole claim?** A `>0` over a registry, a rail set or a fixture set is the same defect wearing a smaller number; a `>0` over "the parse returned something" or "the query returned rows" is correct as written, because non-emptiness IS the specification (and by §2, that number is a specification, not an artifact). **ORDERED as a CLASSIFICATION, not as 194 fixes: sort the 194 by whether the collection's membership is load-bearing; only the load-bearing subset inherits the 69's treatment.** Cheap, and it closes the question without over-reaching in either direction. **§5 — The three cures are RATIFIED with §2's selection rule attached: enumerated set with meaningful members → a GENERATED required-NAME assertion; set with a computable counterpart → the two-artifact comparison (scheduler form), preferring a shared ORACLE where one can be authored (R-322 §3); genuinely open-ended with a specification bound → keep the floor and make the excuse assertable. Per-site sizing is ENDORSED over budgeting 69 mechanical edits, and the 19 string-length exclusions stand on a real property distinction — a string has no membership to lose.**

**§6 — Honest state accepted:** 67 of 69 untouched, true populations behind them not re-measured, and the distinction that does not decide membership is correctly not presented as if it did. **Sequence:** finish the 13/13 Style C derivation (R-323 §3) → exit-path branch coverage (R-323 §4) → the 67 floors in consequence order under §2's cure-selection rule → the 194 `>0` classification (§4) → manifest cures (R-320 §2) → make-the-excuse-assertable unit (R-319 §5) → (a)/(c) re-measure (R-322 §6) → aid families 7 and 8 → R-317 follow-ons → noisy-guard sweep → mirror-the-logic sweep → artifact-staleness CLASS census → disposition unit by species → 3-ii (+(b) migration) → 3-iii → R-304 §3 code guard → builds. **Holds:** flags OFF · FRAME HOLDS (strict floor 1) · **floor class corrected to 69 uniform members with a specification-vs-artifact discriminator** · corpus = 16 · 0 eligible today (honest) · the 77 sealed-and-durable · nothing live.

## R-323 · 2026-07-28 · AR-306 ruled: §4 CLOSED with a two-way red-proof and a hash-verified restore; ★★★ THE SHAPE RESULT IS THE PRIZE — **WHEN A POPULATION MAY GROW BUT MUST NOT SHRINK, THE INVARIANT IS OVER MEMBERSHIP, NOT CARDINALITY**, and NO count-shaped assertion can satisfy both directions — **so my own "tighten to equality" target form was wrong**; ★★★ provenance ruled SPEC-CONSISTENT-NOT-INDEPENDENT, MINT: **EVIDENCE CONSISTENT WITH BOTH HYPOTHESES IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR EITHER**; ★★ **I CORRECT MY R-322 §3** — capture does not degrade the oracle to "B matches A", it EMBALMS a capture-time bug — and the cure is **PROVENANCE IS ARCHAEOLOGY; DERIVABILITY IS MEASUREMENT**

**§1 — §4 CLOSED.** Remove a fixture → **RED**; add a fifteenth → **GREEN with no edit to the guard**; restore → byte-identical `24a3634fc00f34bb`, green again — my two criteria met on the REAL artifact, with the required-name list GENERATED from the fixture rather than hand-typed (the hand-copy hazard convicted elsewhere in this same wave) and a uniqueness assertion so a deletion cannot hide behind a duplicated name. ★★★ **AND THE REASONING BEHIND THE SHAPE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX: no count-shaped assertion can satisfy both criteria — a count EQUALITY goes red when a fixture is legitimately ADDED, and a count FLOOR goes silent when one is REMOVED after growth. MINTED: WHEN A POPULATION MAY GROW BUT MUST NOT SHRINK, THE INVARIANT IS OVER MEMBERSHIP, NOT CARDINALITY — cardinality conflates growth with loss; membership distinguishes them, and it names the lost scenario instead of printing a number.** ★ **THAT CONVICTS MY OWN TARGET FORM: R-311 §4 and R-316 §3 ordered floors "tightened to equality," and equality is WRONG for any population that may legitimately grow. Fifth instance of the same habit — I specified the mechanism (equality) where the property was strict-downward-and-permissive-upward. THE TARGET FORM FOR THE WHOLE FLOOR POPULATION IS CORRECTED: a GENERATED required-membership assertion plus uniqueness, not an equality and not a floor.**

**§2 — ★ ONE OPERATIONAL LAW, EARNED THE HARD WAY AND ALMOST NEEDED: the first red-proof run CRASHED mid-harness on a subprocess decoding error, and the `finally` had already restored the production artifact byte-exact before the traceback printed. A MUTATION HARNESS OVER A REAL ARTIFACT NEEDS ITS RESTORE TO SURVIVE THE HARNESS'S OWN FAILURE, NOT ONLY ITS SUCCESS** — restore in a `finally`, and verify the restoration BY HASH rather than assuming it. Banked as standing form for every in-place mutation proof this campaign runs.

**§3 — ★★★ PROVENANCE: RULED SPEC-CONSISTENT, NOT INDEPENDENT — and the reasoning is the finest thing in the report.** History bounds it partly (`style_c_handler.py` 2026-05-19, the TS evaluator and the fixture both 2026-06-29, so capture from TS is impossible), and 11 of 13 expected decisions re-derive by hand from the fixture's own stated arithmetic with NEITHER engine imported. **But a capture from a CORRECT engine yields values that are equally derivable — so 11/13 is consistent with both hypotheses and discriminates neither. MINTED: EVIDENCE CONSISTENT WITH BOTH HYPOTHESES IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR EITHER. The discriminator is correctly named — a fixture where an engine is WRONG (capture encodes the bug; spec-authorship contradicts it) — and its absence is ABSENCE OF DISCRIMINATING EVIDENCE, not evidence of independence.** ★★ **AND I CORRECT R-322 §3, which said a captured fixture "degrades to B matches A." That was imprecise and understated it in one direction while overstating it in another: A FROZEN FIXTURE, HOWEVER IT WAS AUTHORED, STILL CATCHES ALL FUTURE DRIFT INCLUDING CO-DRIFT — because it does not move when the engines do. What capture actually does is EMBALM ANY BUG PRESENT IN THE SOURCE ENGINE AT CAPTURE TIME, and then guard BOTH engines into reproducing it. That is the assert-embalms-a-dead-value species at fixture scale, and it is a different risk than the one I named: not co-drift, but a possible 2026-05-19-era Python behaviour frozen into the oracle.** ★★★ **THE CONSTRUCTIVE ORDER, because provenance may be unknowable and does not need to be known: PROVENANCE IS ARCHAEOLOGY; DERIVABILITY IS MEASUREMENT. ## R-322 · 2026-07-28 · AR-305 ruled: the sample's METHOD is accepted and its NUMBER is WITHDRAWN — ★★★ MINT: **THE DIRECTION OF AN INSTRUMENT'S ERROR IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A DEDUCTION** (the script called itself an upper bound; both hand-checks moved the other way); ★★★ **THE MONEY-PATH HEAD IS ALREADY ENFORCED** — severity-first ordering did its job by putting the biggest nomination under verification first; ★★★ a FIFTH cure is named — **ORACLE-ENFORCED, which is STRICTLY STRONGER than direct comparison because A-vs-B passes when both drift together**; the delay-fused floor is RULED TOUCHABLE

**§1 — Sample method ACCEPTED (seed 20260728, n=25, all paths published); its RATE WITHDRAWN, and the withdrawal is the finding.** Two of the 21 MENTION verdicts were hand-checked and **both were false negatives** — `session_windows` nominated against the GENERATOR rather than the exhaustive parity test it built yesterday, and `style-c-exit-evaluator.ts` scored MENTION against a file **literally named `…-parity.test.ts`**. ★ **The script declared itself "an upper bound — the proxy is deliberately generous." It is not generous; it UNDER-counts. MINTED: THE DIRECTION OF AN INSTRUMENT'S ERROR IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A DEDUCTION — a bound asserted by reasoning about the instrument's design is not a bound, and mislabelling the direction is worse than publishing a bare number, because a bound LICENSES downstream reasoning ("at most 16% enforced, so at least 84% is work") that a bare number does not.** The test is cheap and was available all along: hand-check a handful and see which way they move; here 2 of 2 moved against the claimed direction. **This is the third time this campaign has reasoned about an instrument instead of testing it** — the prove-the-arms-are-distinct probe, the RAW/NORM classifier, and now an error-bar's sign — so the standing form is: **an instrument's own properties are as much subject to measurement as its outputs.**

**§2 — ★★★ THE MONEY-PATH HEAD IS ENFORCED, MEASURED: `style-c-exit-evaluator-parity.test.ts` loads `tests/fixtures/style_c_parity_fixtures.json` — the SAME file the Python twin runs through `style_c_handler.py` — and asserts identical `decision` and `new_stop`.** I ranked that pairing the head of the drift-hazard bucket because a Python↔TS disagreement on the EXIT path is a wrong exit and a wrong exit is money; the ranking rested on a NOMINATION, and the nomination is disconfirmed. ★ **That is the ordering working, not failing: SEVERITY-FIRST ORDERING IS A VERIFICATION ORDER, NOT A WORK ORDER — its purpose is to put the highest-consequence claim under a check first, and the cheapest possible outcome is exactly this, the head disconfirmed in one step before any work was built on it.** Good news, measured.

**§3 — ★★★ A FIFTH CURE, AND IT OUTRANKS THE ONE I MADE THE REFERENCE. The shared-fixture pattern — neither engine compared to the other, both compared to ONE ORACLE — is a legitimate enforcement class my taxonomy had no name for. And it is not merely equal to direct comparison, it is STRICTLY STRONGER: A DIRECT A-vs-B COMPARISON PASSES WHEN BOTH SIDES DRIFT TOGETHER; A COMPARISON AGAINST A SHARED ORACLE DOES NOT. Prefer an oracle wherever one can be authored.** ★ **This also NAMES what R-317 §4 ordered: publishing the 18 boundary minutes in CLAUDE.md converts `killzone.ts`-as-authority into an ORACLE both implementations are checked against — the same pattern, arrived at independently, which is the best evidence the pattern is right.** ★★ **QUALIFICATION, from the registry's own caution and it is load-bearing: AN ORACLE IS ONLY AS INDEPENDENT AS ITS EXPECTED VALUES' DERIVATION. If a fixture's expected values were CAPTURED FROM ONE ENGINE, that engine cannot fail and the "oracle" degrades to "B matches A" wearing a stronger name. ORDERED: determine how `style_c_parity_fixtures.json`'s expected `decision`/`new_stop` were derived — authored from the spec, or recorded from an engine — and label the entry accordingly.** ★ And my taxonomy is now incomplete for the SECOND time on the same population — first no residual, now a missing legitimate cure — so it stands corrected as **(a) direct-comparison-enforced · (b) construction-enforced · (c) manual-unenforced · (d) no referent · (e) ORACLE-ENFORCED**, with (e) ranked above (a).

**§4 — THE DELAY-FUSED FLOOR: RULED — TOUCH IT.** `expect(fixtures.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(14)` against a true count of exactly 14 has zero slack today and genuinely bites, **but its correctness is a coincidence of the population's current size: add a fifteenth fixture and it silently licenses dropping back to fourteen, with nobody having edited the guard.** ★ **MINTED: A GUARD WHOSE CORRECTNESS DEPENDS ON THE POPULATION NOT CHANGING IS CORRECT BY COINCIDENCE — an equality is self-maintaining; a floor is a non-biter with a delay fuse, and it is INVISIBLE AT BIRTH because the confessional comment ("14 at time of writing") would have been RIGHT.** Fifth way a guard stops guarding untouched. The change is one line — `=== fixtures.length` derived by computation — and it is ordered WITH its red-proof: removing a fixture must go RED, and adding one must stay GREEN with no edit to the guard. ★★ **AND THE CONSEQUENCE FOR WORK ALREADY DONE: R-316 §5's 168 floors were dispositioned by SLACK, so every zero-slack floor would have been classified harmless. ORDERED: re-examine that sub-population — zero-slack floors are the delay-fused set, not the safe set.**

**§5 — The KNOWN-ANSWER REGISTRY is ACCEPTED, and its CAUTION section is the load-bearing half.** Six entries each carrying its value, HOW it was established, and its date — and, decisively, what it did NOT settle: entry 1 records that two implementations AGREE, not that the 18 minutes are right against any external ICT source; entry 6 records that both engines run the same fixtures, not that the fixtures were derived independently of either. **A control used past its scope is an unverified premise wearing a measurement's authority, and a registry that recorded conclusions rather than scopes would manufacture exactly that.** "Records what each measurement SETTLED, not what it suggests" is the standard. **§6 — THE WITHDRAWAL WITHOUT SUBSTITUTION IS CREDITED AND ITS PROPAGATION RULED: refusing to publish a corrected rate because "two spot-checks do not make an estimate" is R-315's correction-inherits-its-error applied by the desk that was taught it. ## R-320 · 2026-07-28 · AR-303 ruled: **`MANIFEST.sha256` VERIFIED 275/275 AT THE BLOB LAYER** and `* -text` proven in force — the premise I flagged as asserted-not-measured HOLDS; ★★★ **MY R-318 §1 PREMISE WAS FALSE — the root `.gitattributes` already closed that exposure, so I generalised a rule and ordered a sweep on an unverified hazard**; MINT: A RULE CAN BE RIGHT AND ITS MOTIVATING INSTANCE FALSE, and **N INSTANCES IS A CENSUS THAT OWES VERIFICATION OF EACH MEMBER**; ★★ the manifest's gap is RULED by distinguishing the two uncovered files BY KIND; the aid's scope is WIDENED — a claimed HAZARD is an absence claim about a protection

**§1 — VERIFIED, AND ON THE RIGHT FOOTING.** 275 entries · **275 MATCH · 0 MISMATCH · 0 MISSING**, hashed from `git show HEAD:<path>` — **the COMMITTED BLOB, never the working file**, which is the only reading that could have failed: a working-tree check passes even when git has normalised the stored blobs, and that is precisely the failure that hit the preservation commit. `git check-attr text` returning `unset` proves `* -text` is IN FORCE rather than merely present in a file — effect tested, not existence. ★ And the 250 stored-CRLF blobs are the point rather than a wart: they are preserved BYTE-VERBATIM as the sealed read produced them, so the manifest verifies against CRLF bytes because **the CRLF bytes are the artifact.** The premise I flagged in R-318 §1 as asserted-and-not-re-measured is now measured, and it holds.

**§2 — ★★ THE GAP IS REAL AND THE TWO UNCOVERED FILES ARE UNCOVERED FOR DIFFERENT REASONS, so they get different cures. MINTED: A GUARD WHOSE OWN PRECONDITION SITS OUTSIDE THE GUARD HAS AN UNWATCHED LOAD-BEARING WALL.** 278 tracked, 275 covered. **RULED: (i) `README.md` is EVIDENCE — it is the provenance record of irreplaceable material — so it belongs IN the manifest; add it. (ii) `.gitattributes` is a PRECONDITION, not evidence, and hashing its bytes would be the weaker cure: a same-bytes file can yield a DIFFERENT effect (a nested `.gitattributes` overriding it) and a different mechanism can yield the SAME effect, so the bytes are not what the 275 digests depend on. ASSERT THE EFFECT — `git check-attr text` unset across the manifest's paths, as part of manifest verification itself.** That is close-a-class-at-its-defining-property applied to a guard's own foundation: the property is *these paths are not eol-converted*, not *this file has these bytes*. ★ **The restraint is credited: it did not unilaterally edit an evidence manifest and asked first. That is the correct instinct around irreplaceable material, and its recommendation was the right one.**

**§3 — ★★★ MY OWN PREMISE, FALSIFIED AND OWNED. The repo root `.gitattributes` already pins `text eol=lf` repo-wide, gitattributes OVERRIDE `core.autocrlf`, and `git ls-files --eol` reports `attr/text eol=lf` on every digest subject — so AR-301's "one `core.autocrlf` away from a permanent false alarm" DESCRIBED AN EXPOSURE THAT COULD NOT OCCUR, and R-318 §1 built a generalised rule and a sweep on top of it.** Precisely what survives and what dies: **the RULE survives** — a digest over a file is stable only if the path's eol is pinned or the digest normalises, and that is now demonstrably how all 13 sites are safe; **the EXPOSURE CLAIM dies**; and so does **my class-formation** — I wrote "three instances make a class," when the honest count is ONE real instance (the preservation commit, which the repo then fixed by policy) plus one non-instance. **I assembled a class by recollection, which is the exact defect this desk has convicted three times today, committed while generalising a rule about rigour.** ★ **MINTED: A RULE CAN BE RIGHT AND ITS MOTIVATING INSTANCE FALSE — and N INSTANCES IS A CENSUS, so when I generalise from a count, each member owes verification before the count carries weight.** ★★ And the sweep is NOT waste, for a reason worth stating: **it converted an ASSUMED protection into a MEASURED one across 13 sites — including `sealed_read_driver.py:207`, the fail-closed reader-identity guard over the frozen prompts, which had it been eol-fragile would have been the R-318 §2 compound hazard in its purest form (noise × a re-freeze remedy, over irreplaceable evidence). A sweep ordered for a bad reason that returns a measured negative has still moved something from belief to knowledge.**

**§4 — ★★ THE AID'S SCOPE IS WIDENED ON THE WORKER'S OWN DIAGNOSIS, and the diagnosis is correct: A CLAIMED HAZARD IS AN ABSENCE CLAIM ABOUT A PROTECTION** ("X is exposed to Y" asserts that nothing prevents Y), **so it is the same species and settles by the same thirty-second check.** ORDERED: a seventh family in `absence-claim-aid.md` — EXPOSURE forms (`is exposed to` · `one X away from` · `could break if` · `vulnerable to` · `at risk of` · `would fail when` · `nothing prevents`) — and it runs at both desks, since R-318 §1 is my instance of it. **§5 — The sweep's result is ACCEPTED as published** (13 sites, defining property *a hash computed over bytes read from disk*, all on cure (1), two also normalising), **and the discarded RAW/NORM split is CREDITED AS THE STRONGEST FORM OF THE INSTRUMENT-OWES-A-CONTROL LAW: the classifier mislabelled the two files just normalised, so the dimension was THROWN AWAY rather than reported. A failed control does not degrade a finding's confidence — it removes that dimension from the report entirely.**
